1	defmodule ReqCassette.Plug do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  A Plug that intercepts Req HTTP requests and records/replays them from cassette files.
4	
5	  This module implements the `Plug` behaviour and is designed to be used with Req's
6	  `:plug` option to enable VCR-style testing for HTTP clients.
7	
8	  ## Usage
9	
10	  The easiest way to use this plug is via the `ReqCassette.with_cassette/3` function,
11	  but it can also be used directly with Req:
12	
13	      # With with_cassette/3 (recommended)
14	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("my_api_call", [cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"], fn plug ->
15	        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
16	      end)
17	
18	      # Direct usage
19	      Req.get!(
20	        "https://api.example.com/data",
21	        plug: {ReqCassette.Plug, %{
22	          cassette_name: "my_api_call",
23	          cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"
24	        }}
25	      )
26	
27	  > #### Cassette Naming Best Practice {: .warning}
28	  >
29	  > Always provide `:cassette_name` for human-readable, maintainable cassette files.
30	  >
31	  > **Without cassette_name** (not recommended):
32	  >
33	  >     plug: {ReqCassette.Plug, %{cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"}}
34	  >     # Creates: a1b2c3d4e5f6789012345678901234ab.json
35	  >     # ❌ Cryptic MD5 hash - hard to identify which test this belongs to
36	  >
37	  > **With cassette_name** (recommended):
38	  >
39	  >     plug: {ReqCassette.Plug, %{cassette_name: "github_user", cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"}}
40	  >     # Creates: github_user.json
41	  >     # ✅ Clear, readable - easy to manage and understand
42	  >
43	  > The MD5 hash fallback exists for backward compatibility but should be avoided in new code.
44	
45	  ## Options
46	
47	  - `:cassette_name` - **(Recommended)** Human-readable name for the cassette file (e.g., `"github_api"`).
48	    Creates `github_api.json`. If omitted, generates a cryptic MD5 hash filename based on
49	    matching options (`:mode`, `:cassette_dir`, and `:cassette_name` are excluded from hash).
50	    **Always provide this option for maintainable tests.**
51	  - `:cassette_dir` - Directory where cassette files are stored (default: `"cassettes"`)
52	  - `:mode` - Recording mode (default: `:record`). See "Recording Modes" below.
53	  - `:match_requests_on` - List of criteria for matching requests (default: `[:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]`)
54	  - `:filter_sensitive_data` - List of `{regex, replacement}` tuples to filter sensitive data
55	  - `:filter_request_headers` - List of request header names to remove (case-insensitive)
56	  - `:filter_response_headers` - List of response header names to remove (case-insensitive)
57	  - `:before_record` - Callback function for custom filtering (receives and returns interaction map)
58	
59	  ## Recording Modes
60	
61	  ReqCassette supports three recording modes that control when cassettes are created/used:
62	
63	  ### `:record` (default)
64	
65	  Records new interactions, replays existing ones. Appends to existing cassettes.
66	  Ideal for development:
67	
68	      # First run: records interaction to cassette
69	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("api", [], fn plug ->
70	        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
71	      end)
72	
73	      # Subsequent runs: replays from cassette (no network call)
74	
75	      # To re-record: delete cassette file first
76	      File.rm!("test/cassettes/api.json")
77	
78	  ### `:replay`
79	
80	  Only replays from cassettes. Raises error if cassette or matching interaction not found.
81	  Perfect for CI environments to ensure no unexpected network calls:
82	
83	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("api", [mode: :replay], fn plug ->
84	        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
85	        # Raises if cassette doesn't exist or no matching interaction
86	      end)
87	
88	  ### `:bypass`
89	
90	  Ignores cassettes completely, always hits the network. Never saves. Useful for
91	  debugging or selectively disabling cassettes:
92	
93	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("api", [mode: :bypass], fn plug ->
94	        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
95	        # Always hits network, never creates cassette
96	      end)
97	
98	  ## Request Matching
99	
100	  By default, requests are matched on all criteria (method, URI, query, headers, body).
101	  You can customize this with `:match_requests_on`:
102	
103	      # Only match on method and URI (ignore query params and body)
104	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
105	        "search",
106	        [match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]],
107	        fn plug ->
108	          Req.get!("https://api.example.com/search?q=foo", plug: plug)
109	          # Later: ?q=bar will replay the same response
110	        end
111	      )
112	
113	  Available matchers:
114	  - `:method` - HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
115	  - `:uri` - Path without query string
116	  - `:query` - Query parameters (order-independent)
117	  - `:headers` - Request headers (case-insensitive)
118	  - `:body` - Request body (JSON key order-independent)
119	
120	  ## Cassette File Format
121	
122	  Cassettes use v1.0 format with pretty-printed JSON and multiple interactions:
123	
124	      {
125	        "version": "1.0",
126	        "interactions": [
127	          {
128	            "request": {
129	              "method": "GET",
130	              "uri": "/api/users/1",
131	              "query_string": "",
132	              "headers": {
133	                "accept": ["application/json"]
134	              },
135	              "body": ""
136	            },
137	            "response": {
138	              "status": 200,
139	              "headers": {
140	                "content-type": ["application/json"]
141	              },
142	              "body_json": {
143	                "id": 1,
144	                "name": "Alice"
145	              }
146	            },
147	            "recorded_at": "2025-10-16T12:00:00Z"
148	          }
149	        ]
150	      }
151	
152	  ### Body Types
153	
154	  Responses are stored in one of three formats based on content type:
155	
156	  - `body_json` - JSON responses stored as native objects (pretty-printed)
157	  - `body` - Text responses (HTML, XML, CSV) stored as strings
158	  - `body_blob` - Binary data (images, PDFs) stored as base64
159	
160	  This approach produces compact, human-readable cassette files.
161	
162	  ## Examples
163	
164	      # Basic GET request with human-readable filename
165	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("github_user", [], fn plug ->
166	        Req.get!("https://api.github.com/users/octocat", plug: plug)
167	      end)
168	      # Creates: test/cassettes/github_user.json
169	
170	      # POST with custom matching (ignore request body)
171	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
172	        "create_user",
173	        [match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]],
174	        fn plug ->
175	          Req.post!(
176	            "https://api.example.com/users",
177	            json: %{name: "Alice"},
178	            plug: plug
179	          )
180	        end
181	      )
182	
183	      # Filter sensitive data with regex
184	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
185	        "authenticated",
186	        [
187	          filter_sensitive_data: [
188	            {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"}
189	          ],
190	          filter_request_headers: ["authorization"]
191	        ],
192	        fn plug ->
193	          Req.get!(
194	            "https://api.example.com/data?api_key=secret",
195	            headers: [{"authorization", "Bearer token"}],
196	            plug: plug
197	          )
198	        end
199	      )
200	
201	      # Multiple requests in one cassette
202	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("workflow", [], fn plug ->
203	        user = Req.get!("https://api.example.com/user", plug: plug)
204	        posts = Req.get!("https://api.example.com/posts", plug: plug)
205	        {user, posts}
206	      end)
207	      # Single cassette file contains both interactions
208	
209	      # Custom filtering with callback
210	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
211	        "custom_filter",
212	        [
213	          before_record: fn interaction ->
214	            put_in(interaction, ["response", "body_json", "email"], "redacted@example.com")
215	          end
216	        ],
217	        fn plug ->
218	          Req.get!("https://api.example.com/profile", plug: plug)
219	        end
220	      )
221	
222	  ## Architecture
223	
224	  This plug uses Req's native plug system, which provides:
225	
226	  - ✅ **Async-safe**: Works with `async: true` in ExUnit
227	  - ✅ **Process-isolated**: No global state or process dictionary
228	  - ✅ **Adapter-agnostic**: Works with any Req adapter (Finch, etc.)
229	  - ✅ **No mocking**: Uses stable, public APIs
230	
231	  ## How It Works
232	
233	  1. **Recording Flow** (`:record` mode):
234	     - Intercepts the outgoing Req request via the plug callback
235	     - Checks if a matching cassette/interaction exists
236	     - If not found, forwards the request to the real server
237	     - Applies filters to remove sensitive data
238	     - Saves the response to a cassette file (pretty-printed JSON)
239	     - Returns the response to the caller
240	
241	  2. **Replay Flow** (`:replay` or `:record` with existing cassette):
242	     - Intercepts the outgoing request
243	     - Finds the matching cassette file by name
244	     - Searches for a matching interaction using configured matchers
245	     - Loads and returns the saved response
246	     - No network call is made
247	
248	  3. **Bypass Flow** (`:bypass` mode):
249	     - Forwards request directly to the network
250	     - Never reads or writes cassettes
251	     - Useful for debugging or selectively disabling recording
252	
253	  ## Integration with ReqLLM
254	
255	  Works seamlessly with ReqLLM for testing LLM integrations:
256	
257	      ReqCassette.with_cassette("claude_chat", [], fn plug ->
258	        ReqLLM.chat(
259	          "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
260	          [%{role: "user", content: "Hello!"}],
261	          req_http_options: [plug: plug]
262	        )
263	      end)

279	  - `:cassette_name` - Human-readable name for the cassette file
280	  - `:mode` - Recording mode (`:replay`, `:record`, `:bypass`)
281	  - `:match_requests_on` - List of matchers for finding interactions
282	  """
283	  @type opts :: %{

296	  @doc """
297	  Initializes the plug with the given options.
298	
299	  This callback is invoked by Req when the plug is first used. It merges the provided
300	  options with default values to create the final configuration.
301	
302	  ## Parameters
303	
304	  - `opts` - A map of options (see `t:opts/0`)
305	
306	  ## Returns
307	
308	  The merged options map with defaults applied.
309	
310	  ## Default Options
311	
312	  - `cassette_dir: "cassettes"` - Directory for storing cassette files
313	  - `mode: :record` - Record new interactions, replay existing ones
314	  - `match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]` - Match on all criteria
315	
316	  ## Examples
317	
318	      # Minimal options (uses defaults)
319	      opts = %{cassette_name: "my_api"}
320	      ReqCassette.Plug.init(opts)
321	      #=> %{
322	      #     cassette_name: "my_api",
323	      #     cassette_dir: "cassettes",
324	      #     mode: :record,
325	      #     match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
326	      #   }
327	
328	      # Custom options override defaults
329	      opts = %{
330	        cassette_name: "my_api",
331	        mode: :replay,
332	        match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]
333	      }
334	      ReqCassette.Plug.init(opts)
335	      #=> %{
336	      #     cassette_name: "my_api",
337	      #     cassette_dir: "cassettes",
338	      #     mode: :replay,
339	      #     match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]
340	      #   }
341	  """
342	  @spec init(opts() | map()) :: opts()
343	  def init(opts) do
344	    Map.merge(@default_opts, opts)
345	  end

347	  @doc """
348	  Handles an incoming HTTP request by either replaying from cassette or recording.
349	
350	  This is the main entry point for the plug, called by Req for each HTTP request.
351	  The behavior depends on the configured mode:
352	
353	  - **`:record`** (default) - Checks for matching interaction, records if not found
354	  - **`:replay`** - Only uses cassettes, raises error if not found
355	  - **`:bypass`** - Ignores cassettes, always uses network
356	
357	  ## Parameters
358	
359	  - `conn` - The `Plug.Conn` struct representing the incoming request
360	  - `opts` - The plug options (see `t:opts/0`)
361	
362	  ## Returns
363	
364	  A `Plug.Conn` struct with the response set and halted.
365	
366	  ## Request Matching
367	
368	  When looking for a matching interaction in an existing cassette, the plug uses
369	  the matchers specified in `:match_requests_on`. For example:
370	
371	  - `[:method, :uri]` - Match only method and path (ignore query params and body)
372	  - `[:method, :uri, :query]` - Match method, path, and query params
373	  - `[:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]` - Match everything (default)
374	
375	  Query parameters and JSON body keys are normalized (order-independent) to ensure
376	  consistent matching.
377	
378	  ## Filtering
379	
380	  Before recording, the plug applies filters in this order:
381	
382	  1. **Regex filters** (`:filter_sensitive_data`) - Applied to URI, query string, and bodies
383	  2. **Header filters** (`:filter_request_headers`, `:filter_response_headers`) - Removes specified headers
384	  3. **Callback filter** (`:before_record`) - Custom transformation function
385	
386	  ## Examples
387	
388	      # Direct plug usage with replay mode (CI environment)
389	      plug_opts = %{
390	        cassette_name: "github_api",
391	        cassette_dir: "test/cassettes",
392	        mode: :replay
393	      }
394	
395	      conn = %Plug.Conn{
396	        method: "GET",
397	        request_path: "/users/octocat",
398	        # ... other fields
399	      }
400	
401	      # Raises if cassette doesn't exist
402	      conn = ReqCassette.Plug.call(conn, plug_opts)
403	
404	      # With custom matching (ignore body differences)
405	      plug_opts = %{
406	        cassette_name: "api_call",
407	        match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query]
408	      }
409	
410	      conn = ReqCassette.Plug.call(conn, plug_opts)
411	      # POST requests with different bodies will match the same interaction
412	
413	      # With filtering
414	      plug_opts = %{
415	        cassette_name: "auth_api",
416	        filter_sensitive_data: [
417	          {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"}
418	        ],
419	        filter_request_headers: ["authorization"]
420	      }
421	
422	      conn = ReqCassette.Plug.call(conn, plug_opts)
423	      # API keys in query string are redacted, authorization headers removed
424	
425	  ## Errors
426	
427	  This function raises in the following cases:
428	
429	  - **Mode `:replay`** with missing cassette
430	  - **Mode `:replay`** with no matching interaction
431	  - **Mode `:record`** when network request fails
432	
433	  The error messages include context to help debug the issue.
434	  """
435	  @spec call(Conn.t(), opts()) :: Conn.t()
436	  def call(conn, opts) do
437	    # Read the body first so we can include it in the cassette key
438	    conn = Conn.fetch_query_params(conn)
439	    {:ok, body, conn} = Conn.read_body(conn)
440	
441	    # Handle different recording modes
442	    case opts.mode do
443	      :bypass ->
444	        # Bypass mode - ignore cassettes, always hit network
445	        {conn, resp_or_error} = forward_and_capture(conn, body, opts)
446	        resp = normalize_response(resp_or_error)
447	        resp_to_conn(conn, resp)
448	
449	      :replay ->
450	        # Replay mode - only use cassettes, error if missing
451	        handle_replay(conn, body, opts)
452	
453	      :record ->
454	        # Record mode - use cassette if exists, otherwise record (append interactions)
455	        handle_record(conn, body, opts)
456	    end
457	  end
458	
459	  # Mode handlers
460	
461	  defp handle_replay(conn, body, opts) do
462	    path = cassette_path(opts)
463	
464	    case Cassette.load(path) do
465	      {:ok, cassette} ->
466	        match_on = opts[:match_requests_on] || [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
467	        filter_opts = extract_filter_opts(opts)
468	        filtered_request = build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts)
469	
470	        case find_matching_interaction_replay(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
471	          {:ok, response} ->
472	            send_cached_response(conn, response)
473	
474	          :not_found ->
475	            raise_no_match_error(cassette, conn, body, match_on, filter_opts, path)
476	        end
477	
478	      :not_found ->
479	        raise """
480	        ReqCassette: Cassette not found: #{path}
481	
482	        Mode is :replay which requires an existing cassette.
483	        Either create the cassette or use mode: :record.
484	        """
485	    end
486	  end
487	
488	  defp handle_record(conn, body, opts) do
489	    path = cassette_path(opts)
490	
491	    case Cassette.load(path) do
492	      {:ok, cassette} ->
493	        handle_record_with_existing_cassette(conn, body, opts, cassette, path)
494	
495	      :not_found ->
496	        handle_record_new_cassette(conn, body, opts, path)
497	    end
498	  end
499	
500	  defp handle_record_with_existing_cassette(conn, body, opts, cassette, path) do
501	    match_on = opts[:match_requests_on] || [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
502	    filter_opts = extract_filter_opts(opts)
503	    filtered_request = build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts)
504	
505	    case find_matching_interaction_record(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
506	      {:ok, response} ->
507	        send_cached_response(conn, response)
508	
509	      :not_found ->
510	        record_new_interaction(conn, body, opts, cassette, filtered_request, path)
511	    end
512	  end
513	
514	  defp handle_record_new_cassette(conn, body, opts, path) do
515	    filter_opts = extract_filter_opts(opts)
516	    filtered_request = build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts)
517	
518	    record_new_interaction(conn, body, opts, Cassette.new(), filtered_request, path)
519	  end
520	
521	  defp record_new_interaction(conn, body, opts, cassette, filtered_request, path) do
522	    {conn, resp_or_error} = forward_and_capture(conn, body, opts)
523	    resp = normalize_response(resp_or_error)
524	
525	    cassette = Cassette.add_interaction(cassette, filtered_request, resp, opts)
526	    Cassette.save(path, cassette)
527	
528	    maybe_advance_session(path, opts)
529	    resp_to_conn(conn, resp)
530	  end
531	
532	  # Sequential matching helpers
533	
534	  # For replay mode: use atomic get-and-advance for concurrent safety
535	  defp find_matching_interaction_replay(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
536	    case opts[:session_id] do
537	      nil ->
538	        # No session: use traditional scanning (backward compatible behavior)
539	        Cassette.find_interaction(cassette, filtered_request, match_on)
540	
541	      session_id ->
542	        # With session: use strict sequential matching
543	        # Atomic get-and-advance ensures each concurrent request gets a unique index
544	        start_index = Session.get_and_advance_index(path, session_id)
545	
546	        Cassette.find_interaction_sequential(
547	          cassette,
548	          filtered_request,
549	          match_on,
550	          start_index
551	        )
552	        |> case do
553	          {:ok, response, _matched_index} -> {:ok, response}
554	          :not_found -> :not_found
555	        end
556	    end
557	  end
558	
559	  # For record mode: don't advance atomically (advance happens after recording)
560	  defp find_matching_interaction_record(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
561	    case opts[:session_id] do
562	      nil ->
563	        # No session: use traditional scanning (backward compatible behavior)
564	        Cassette.find_interaction(cassette, filtered_request, match_on)
565	
566	      session_id ->
567	        # With session: use strict sequential matching
568	        start_index = Session.get_current_index(path, session_id)
569	
570	        Cassette.find_interaction_sequential(
571	          cassette,
572	          filtered_request,
573	          match_on,
574	          start_index
575	        )
576	        |> case do
577	          {:ok, response, _matched_index} ->
578	            # Advance after successful match
579	            Session.advance_index(path, session_id)
580	            {:ok, response}
581	
582	          :not_found ->
583	            :not_found
584	        end
585	    end

defmodule ReqCassette.Plug do
  @moduledoc """
  A Plug that intercepts Req HTTP requests and records/replays them from cassette files.

  This module implements the `Plug` behaviour and is designed to be used with Req's
  `:plug` option to enable VCR-style testing for HTTP clients.

  ## Usage

  The easiest way to use this plug is via the `ReqCassette.with_cassette/3` function,
  but it can also be used directly with Req:

      # With with_cassette/3 (recommended)
      ReqCassette.with_cassette("my_api_call", [cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"], fn plug ->
        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
      end)

      # Direct usage
      Req.get!(
        "https://api.example.com/data",
        plug: {ReqCassette.Plug, %{
          cassette_name: "my_api_call",
          cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"
        }}
      )

  > #### Cassette Naming Best Practice {: .warning}
  >
  > Always provide `:cassette_name` for human-readable, maintainable cassette files.
  >
  > **Without cassette_name** (not recommended):
  >
  >     plug: {ReqCassette.Plug, %{cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"}}
  >     # Creates: a1b2c3d4e5f6789012345678901234ab.json
  >     # ❌ Cryptic MD5 hash - hard to identify which test this belongs to
  >
  > **With cassette_name** (recommended):
  >
  >     plug: {ReqCassette.Plug, %{cassette_name: "github_user", cassette_dir: "test/cassettes"}}
  >     # Creates: github_user.json
  >     # ✅ Clear, readable - easy to manage and understand
  >
  > The MD5 hash fallback exists for backward compatibility but should be avoided in new code.

  ## Options

  - `:cassette_name` - **(Recommended)** Human-readable name for the cassette file (e.g., `"github_api"`).
    Creates `github_api.json`. If omitted, generates a cryptic MD5 hash filename based on
    matching options (`:mode`, `:cassette_dir`, and `:cassette_name` are excluded from hash).
    **Always provide this option for maintainable tests.**
  - `:cassette_dir` - Directory where cassette files are stored (default: `"cassettes"`)
  - `:mode` - Recording mode (default: `:record`). See "Recording Modes" below.
  - `:match_requests_on` - List of criteria for matching requests (default: `[:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]`)
  - `:filter_sensitive_data` - List of `{regex, replacement}` tuples to filter sensitive data
  - `:filter_request_headers` - List of request header names to remove (case-insensitive)
  - `:filter_response_headers` - List of response header names to remove (case-insensitive)
  - `:before_record` - Callback function for custom filtering (receives and returns interaction map)

  ## Recording Modes

  ReqCassette supports three recording modes that control when cassettes are created/used:

  ### `:record` (default)

  Records new interactions, replays existing ones. Appends to existing cassettes.
  Ideal for development:

      # First run: records interaction to cassette
      ReqCassette.with_cassette("api", [], fn plug ->
        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
      end)

      # Subsequent runs: replays from cassette (no network call)

      # To re-record: delete cassette file first
      File.rm!("test/cassettes/api.json")

  ### `:replay`

  Only replays from cassettes. Raises error if cassette or matching interaction not found.
  Perfect for CI environments to ensure no unexpected network calls:

      ReqCassette.with_cassette("api", [mode: :replay], fn plug ->
        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
        # Raises if cassette doesn't exist or no matching interaction
      end)

  ### `:bypass`

  Ignores cassettes completely, always hits the network. Never saves. Useful for
  debugging or selectively disabling cassettes:

      ReqCassette.with_cassette("api", [mode: :bypass], fn plug ->
        Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data", plug: plug)
        # Always hits network, never creates cassette
      end)

  ## Request Matching

  By default, requests are matched on all criteria (method, URI, query, headers, body).
  You can customize this with `:match_requests_on`:

      # Only match on method and URI (ignore query params and body)
      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
        "search",
        [match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]],
        fn plug ->
          Req.get!("https://api.example.com/search?q=foo", plug: plug)
          # Later: ?q=bar will replay the same response
        end
      )

  Available matchers:
  - `:method` - HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
  - `:uri` - Path without query string
  - `:query` - Query parameters (order-independent)
  - `:headers` - Request headers (case-insensitive)
  - `:body` - Request body (JSON key order-independent)

  ## Cassette File Format

  Cassettes use v1.0 format with pretty-printed JSON and multiple interactions:

      {
        "version": "1.0",
        "interactions": [
          {
            "request": {
              "method": "GET",
              "uri": "/api/users/1",
              "query_string": "",
              "headers": {
                "accept": ["application/json"]
              },
              "body": ""
            },
            "response": {
              "status": 200,
              "headers": {
                "content-type": ["application/json"]
              },
              "body_json": {
                "id": 1,
                "name": "Alice"
              }
            },
            "recorded_at": "2025-10-16T12:00:00Z"
          }
        ]
      }

  ### Body Types

  Responses are stored in one of three formats based on content type:

  - `body_json` - JSON responses stored as native objects (pretty-printed)
  - `body` - Text responses (HTML, XML, CSV) stored as strings
  - `body_blob` - Binary data (images, PDFs) stored as base64

  This approach produces compact, human-readable cassette files.

  ## Examples

      # Basic GET request with human-readable filename
      ReqCassette.with_cassette("github_user", [], fn plug ->
        Req.get!("https://api.github.com/users/octocat", plug: plug)
      end)
      # Creates: test/cassettes/github_user.json

      # POST with custom matching (ignore request body)
      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
        "create_user",
        [match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]],
        fn plug ->
          Req.post!(
            "https://api.example.com/users",
            json: %{name: "Alice"},
            plug: plug
          )
        end
      )

      # Filter sensitive data with regex
      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
        "authenticated",
        [
          filter_sensitive_data: [
            {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"}
          ],
          filter_request_headers: ["authorization"]
        ],
        fn plug ->
          Req.get!(
            "https://api.example.com/data?api_key=secret",
            headers: [{"authorization", "Bearer token"}],
            plug: plug
          )
        end
      )

      # Multiple requests in one cassette
      ReqCassette.with_cassette("workflow", [], fn plug ->
        user = Req.get!("https://api.example.com/user", plug: plug)
        posts = Req.get!("https://api.example.com/posts", plug: plug)
        {user, posts}
      end)
      # Single cassette file contains both interactions

      # Custom filtering with callback
      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
        "custom_filter",
        [
          before_record: fn interaction ->
            put_in(interaction, ["response", "body_json", "email"], "redacted@example.com")
          end
        ],
        fn plug ->
          Req.get!("https://api.example.com/profile", plug: plug)
        end
      )

  ## Architecture

  This plug uses Req's native plug system, which provides:

  - ✅ **Async-safe**: Works with `async: true` in ExUnit
  - ✅ **Process-isolated**: No global state or process dictionary
  - ✅ **Adapter-agnostic**: Works with any Req adapter (Finch, etc.)
  - ✅ **No mocking**: Uses stable, public APIs

  ## How It Works

  1. **Recording Flow** (`:record` mode):
     - Intercepts the outgoing Req request via the plug callback
     - Checks if a matching cassette/interaction exists
     - If not found, forwards the request to the real server
     - Applies filters to remove sensitive data
     - Saves the response to a cassette file (pretty-printed JSON)
     - Returns the response to the caller

  2. **Replay Flow** (`:replay` or `:record` with existing cassette):
     - Intercepts the outgoing request
     - Finds the matching cassette file by name
     - Searches for a matching interaction using configured matchers
     - Loads and returns the saved response
     - No network call is made

  3. **Bypass Flow** (`:bypass` mode):
     - Forwards request directly to the network
     - Never reads or writes cassettes
     - Useful for debugging or selectively disabling recording

  ## Integration with ReqLLM

  Works seamlessly with ReqLLM for testing LLM integrations:

      ReqCassette.with_cassette("claude_chat", [], fn plug ->
        ReqLLM.chat(
          "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
          [%{role: "user", content: "Hello!"}],
          req_http_options: [plug: plug]
        )
      end)
  """
  @behaviour Plug

  import Plug.Conn

  alias Plug.Conn
  alias Req.Steps
  alias ReqCassette.BodyType
  alias ReqCassette.Cassette
  alias ReqCassette.Session

  @typedoc """
  Options for configuring the cassette plug.

  - `:cassette_dir` - Directory where cassette files are stored
  - `:cassette_name` - Human-readable name for the cassette file
  - `:mode` - Recording mode (`:replay`, `:record`, `:bypass`)
  - `:match_requests_on` - List of matchers for finding interactions
  """
  @type opts :: %{
          optional(:cassette_name) => String.t(),
          cassette_dir: String.t(),
          mode: :replay | :record | :bypass,
          match_requests_on: [atom()]
        }

  @default_opts %{
    cassette_dir: "cassettes",
    mode: :record,
    match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
  }

  @doc """
  Initializes the plug with the given options.

  This callback is invoked by Req when the plug is first used. It merges the provided
  options with default values to create the final configuration.

  ## Parameters

  - `opts` - A map of options (see `t:opts/0`)

  ## Returns

  The merged options map with defaults applied.

  ## Default Options

  - `cassette_dir: "cassettes"` - Directory for storing cassette files
  - `mode: :record` - Record new interactions, replay existing ones
  - `match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]` - Match on all criteria

  ## Examples

      # Minimal options (uses defaults)
      opts = %{cassette_name: "my_api"}
      ReqCassette.Plug.init(opts)
      #=> %{
      #     cassette_name: "my_api",
      #     cassette_dir: "cassettes",
      #     mode: :record,
      #     match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
      #   }

      # Custom options override defaults
      opts = %{
        cassette_name: "my_api",
        mode: :replay,
        match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]
      }
      ReqCassette.Plug.init(opts)
      #=> %{
      #     cassette_name: "my_api",
      #     cassette_dir: "cassettes",
      #     mode: :replay,
      #     match_requests_on: [:method, :uri]
      #   }
  """
  @spec init(opts() | map()) :: opts()
  def init(opts) do
    Map.merge(@default_opts, opts)
  end

  @doc """
  Handles an incoming HTTP request by either replaying from cassette or recording.

  This is the main entry point for the plug, called by Req for each HTTP request.
  The behavior depends on the configured mode:

  - **`:record`** (default) - Checks for matching interaction, records if not found
  - **`:replay`** - Only uses cassettes, raises error if not found
  - **`:bypass`** - Ignores cassettes, always uses network

  ## Parameters

  - `conn` - The `Plug.Conn` struct representing the incoming request
  - `opts` - The plug options (see `t:opts/0`)

  ## Returns

  A `Plug.Conn` struct with the response set and halted.

  ## Request Matching

  When looking for a matching interaction in an existing cassette, the plug uses
  the matchers specified in `:match_requests_on`. For example:

  - `[:method, :uri]` - Match only method and path (ignore query params and body)
  - `[:method, :uri, :query]` - Match method, path, and query params
  - `[:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]` - Match everything (default)

  Query parameters and JSON body keys are normalized (order-independent) to ensure
  consistent matching.

  ## Filtering

  Before recording, the plug applies filters in this order:

  1. **Regex filters** (`:filter_sensitive_data`) - Applied to URI, query string, and bodies
  2. **Header filters** (`:filter_request_headers`, `:filter_response_headers`) - Removes specified headers
  3. **Callback filter** (`:before_record`) - Custom transformation function

  ## Examples

      # Direct plug usage with replay mode (CI environment)
      plug_opts = %{
        cassette_name: "github_api",
        cassette_dir: "test/cassettes",
        mode: :replay
      }

      conn = %Plug.Conn{
        method: "GET",
        request_path: "/users/octocat",
        # ... other fields
      }

      # Raises if cassette doesn't exist
      conn = ReqCassette.Plug.call(conn, plug_opts)

      # With custom matching (ignore body differences)
      plug_opts = %{
        cassette_name: "api_call",
        match_requests_on: [:method, :uri, :query]
      }

      conn = ReqCassette.Plug.call(conn, plug_opts)
      # POST requests with different bodies will match the same interaction

      # With filtering
      plug_opts = %{
        cassette_name: "auth_api",
        filter_sensitive_data: [
          {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"}
        ],
        filter_request_headers: ["authorization"]
      }

      conn = ReqCassette.Plug.call(conn, plug_opts)
      # API keys in query string are redacted, authorization headers removed

  ## Errors

  This function raises in the following cases:

  - **Mode `:replay`** with missing cassette
  - **Mode `:replay`** with no matching interaction
  - **Mode `:record`** when network request fails

  The error messages include context to help debug the issue.
  """
  @spec call(Conn.t(), opts()) :: Conn.t()
  def call(conn, opts) do
    # Read the body first so we can include it in the cassette key
    conn = Conn.fetch_query_params(conn)
    {:ok, body, conn} = Conn.read_body(conn)

    # Handle different recording modes
    case opts.mode do
      :bypass ->
        # Bypass mode - ignore cassettes, always hit network
        {conn, resp_or_error} = forward_and_capture(conn, body, opts)
        resp = normalize_response(resp_or_error)
        resp_to_conn(conn, resp)

      :replay ->
        # Replay mode - only use cassettes, error if missing
        handle_replay(conn, body, opts)

      :record ->
        # Record mode - use cassette if exists, otherwise record (append interactions)
        handle_record(conn, body, opts)
    end
  end

  # Mode handlers

  defp handle_replay(conn, body, opts) do
    path = cassette_path(opts)

    case Cassette.load(path) do
      {:ok, cassette} ->
        match_on = opts[:match_requests_on] || [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
        filter_opts = extract_filter_opts(opts)
        filtered_request = build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts)

        case find_matching_interaction_replay(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
          {:ok, response} ->
            send_cached_response(conn, response)

          :not_found ->
            raise_no_match_error(cassette, conn, body, match_on, filter_opts, path)
        end

      :not_found ->
        raise """
        ReqCassette: Cassette not found: #{path}

        Mode is :replay which requires an existing cassette.
        Either create the cassette or use mode: :record.
        """
    end
  end

  defp handle_record(conn, body, opts) do
    path = cassette_path(opts)

    case Cassette.load(path) do
      {:ok, cassette} ->
        handle_record_with_existing_cassette(conn, body, opts, cassette, path)

      :not_found ->
        handle_record_new_cassette(conn, body, opts, path)
    end
  end

  defp handle_record_with_existing_cassette(conn, body, opts, cassette, path) do
    match_on = opts[:match_requests_on] || [:method, :uri, :query, :headers, :body]
    filter_opts = extract_filter_opts(opts)
    filtered_request = build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts)

    case find_matching_interaction_record(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
      {:ok, response} ->
        send_cached_response(conn, response)

      :not_found ->
        record_new_interaction(conn, body, opts, cassette, filtered_request, path)
    end
  end

  defp handle_record_new_cassette(conn, body, opts, path) do
    filter_opts = extract_filter_opts(opts)
    filtered_request = build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts)

    record_new_interaction(conn, body, opts, Cassette.new(), filtered_request, path)
  end

  defp record_new_interaction(conn, body, opts, cassette, filtered_request, path) do
    {conn, resp_or_error} = forward_and_capture(conn, body, opts)
    resp = normalize_response(resp_or_error)

    cassette = Cassette.add_interaction(cassette, filtered_request, resp, opts)
    Cassette.save(path, cassette)

    maybe_advance_session(path, opts)
    resp_to_conn(conn, resp)
  end

  # Sequential matching helpers

  # For replay mode: use atomic get-and-advance for concurrent safety
  defp find_matching_interaction_replay(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
    case opts[:session_id] do
      nil ->
        # No session: use traditional scanning (backward compatible behavior)
        Cassette.find_interaction(cassette, filtered_request, match_on)

      session_id ->
        # With session: use strict sequential matching
        # Atomic get-and-advance ensures each concurrent request gets a unique index
        start_index = Session.get_and_advance_index(path, session_id)

        Cassette.find_interaction_sequential(
          cassette,
          filtered_request,
          match_on,
          start_index
        )
        |> case do
          {:ok, response, _matched_index} -> {:ok, response}
          :not_found -> :not_found
        end
    end
  end

  # For record mode: don't advance atomically (advance happens after recording)
  defp find_matching_interaction_record(cassette, filtered_request, match_on, path, opts) do
    case opts[:session_id] do
      nil ->
        # No session: use traditional scanning (backward compatible behavior)
        Cassette.find_interaction(cassette, filtered_request, match_on)

      session_id ->
        # With session: use strict sequential matching
        start_index = Session.get_current_index(path, session_id)

        Cassette.find_interaction_sequential(
          cassette,
          filtered_request,
          match_on,
          start_index
        )
        |> case do
          {:ok, response, _matched_index} ->
            # Advance after successful match
            Session.advance_index(path, session_id)
            {:ok, response}

          :not_found ->
            :not_found
        end
    end
  end

  defp maybe_advance_session(path, opts) do
    if opts[:session_id] do
      Session.advance_index(path, opts[:session_id])
    end
  end

  defp send_cached_response(conn, response) do
    conn
    |> put_resp_headers(response["headers"])
    |> send_resp(response["status"], BodyType.decode(response))
    |> Conn.halt()
  end

  defp raise_no_match_error(cassette, conn, body, match_on, filter_opts, path) do
    diagnostics = Cassette.diagnose_mismatch(cassette, conn, body, match_on, filter_opts)
    diagnostics_str = Cassette.format_mismatch_diagnostics(diagnostics, match_on)

    raise """
    ReqCassette: No matching interaction found in cassette #{path}

    Request: #{conn.method} #{conn.request_path}
    Matching on: #{inspect(match_on)}

    This cassette exists but doesn't contain a matching interaction.
    Either add the interaction to the cassette or use mode: :record.

    #{diagnostics_str}
    """
  end

  defp extract_filter_opts(opts) do
    base_opts = %{
      filter_sensitive_data: opts[:filter_sensitive_data] || [],
      filter_request_headers: opts[:filter_request_headers] || [],
      filter_response_headers: opts[:filter_response_headers] || [],
      filter_request: opts[:filter_request],
      filter_response: opts[:filter_response]
    }

    # Add template options if present
    if opts[:template] do
      Map.put(base_opts, :template, opts[:template])
    else
      base_opts
    end
  end

  # Build and filter incoming request once at entry point
  # This ensures all downstream code (template matching, standard matching) works on filtered data
  defp build_and_filter_incoming_request(conn, body, filter_opts) do
    # 1. Build request structure
    body_type = BodyType.detect_type(body, headers_to_map(conn.req_headers))
    {body_field, body_value} = BodyType.encode(body, body_type)

    request =
      %{
        "method" => conn.method,
        "uri" => build_uri(conn),
        "query_string" => conn.query_string,
        "headers" => headers_to_map(conn.req_headers),
        "body_type" => to_string(body_type)
      }
      |> Map.put(body_field, body_value)

    # 2. Apply ALL filters in order: callback → regex → header removal
    request
    |> apply_filter_request_callback(filter_opts[:filter_request])
    |> apply_regex_filters_to_request(filter_opts[:filter_sensitive_data] || [])
    |> apply_request_header_filters(filter_opts[:filter_request_headers] || [])
  end

  # Apply filter_request callback
  defp apply_filter_request_callback(request, nil), do: request

  defp apply_filter_request_callback(request, callback) when is_function(callback, 1) do
    callback.(request)
  end

  defp apply_filter_request_callback(request, _), do: request

  # Apply regex filters to request body and URI/query
  defp apply_regex_filters_to_request(request, []), do: request

  defp apply_regex_filters_to_request(request, filter_patterns) do
    request
    |> apply_regex_to_body(filter_patterns)
    |> apply_regex_to_uri(filter_patterns)
    |> apply_regex_to_query(filter_patterns)
  end

  defp apply_regex_to_body(request, filter_patterns) do
    cond do
      Map.has_key?(request, "body_json") ->
        # Filter JSON by serializing, filtering, deserializing
        json_str = Jason.encode!(request["body_json"])
        filtered_str = apply_regex_to_string(json_str, filter_patterns)

        # Use tolerant decoding - if regex produces invalid JSON, fall back to original
        # This matches the behavior in ReqCassette.Filter.apply_regex_to_body/3
        filtered_json =
          case Jason.decode(filtered_str) do
            {:ok, decoded} -> decoded
            {:error, _} -> request["body_json"]
          end

        Map.put(request, "body_json", filtered_json)

      Map.has_key?(request, "body") ->
        # Filter plain text body
        filtered_body = apply_regex_to_string(request["body"], filter_patterns)
        Map.put(request, "body", filtered_body)

      Map.has_key?(request, "body_blob") ->
        # Filter blob (decode, filter, re-encode)
        blob = Base.decode64!(request["body_blob"])
        filtered = apply_regex_to_string(blob, filter_patterns)
        Map.put(request, "body_blob", Base.encode64(filtered))

      true ->
        request
    end
  end

  defp apply_regex_to_uri(request, filter_patterns) do
    filtered_uri = apply_regex_to_string(request["uri"], filter_patterns)
    Map.put(request, "uri", filtered_uri)
  end

  defp apply_regex_to_query(request, filter_patterns) do
    filtered_query = apply_regex_to_string(request["query_string"], filter_patterns)
    Map.put(request, "query_string", filtered_query)
  end

  defp apply_regex_to_string(string, filter_patterns) do
    Enum.reduce(filter_patterns, string, fn {pattern, replacement}, acc ->
      String.replace(acc, pattern, replacement)
    end)
  end

  # Apply header filters (remove specified headers)
  defp apply_request_header_filters(request, []), do: request

  defp apply_request_header_filters(request, filter_list) do
    filtered_headers =
      request["headers"]
      |> Enum.reject(fn {key, _value} ->
        Enum.any?(filter_list, &(String.downcase(key) == String.downcase(&1)))
      end)
      |> Enum.into(%{})

    Map.put(request, "headers", filtered_headers)
  end

  defp build_uri(conn) do
    scheme = to_string(conn.scheme || if(conn.port == 443, do: "https", else: "http"))
    host = conn.host || "localhost"
    port = conn.port || 80

    # Only include port if non-standard
    port_str =
      cond do
        scheme == "http" and port == 80 -> ""
        scheme == "https" and port == 443 -> ""
        true -> ":#{port}"
      end

    "#{scheme}://#{host}#{port_str}#{conn.request_path}"
  end

  defp headers_to_map(headers) when is_list(headers) do
    Enum.into(headers, %{}, fn
      {k, v} when is_list(v) -> {k, v}
      {k, v} -> {k, [v]}
    end)
  end

  defp headers_to_map(headers) when is_map(headers), do: headers

  defp cassette_path(opts) do
    dir = opts.cassette_dir || opts[:cassette_dir] || "cassettes"

    filename =
      case opts[:cassette_name] do
        nil ->
          # Generate MD5 hash (backward compatibility)
          # Exclude cassette management options from hash - only hash options that affect matching
          opts_for_hash = Map.drop(opts, [:mode, :cassette_dir, :cassette_name])
          hash = :crypto.hash(:md5, :erlang.term_to_binary(opts_for_hash))
          Base.encode16(hash, case: :lower) <> ".json"

        name ->
          # Use human-readable name
          Cassette.sanitize_filename(name) <> ".json"
      end

    Path.join(dir, filename)
  end

  defp normalize_response(resp_or_error) do
    case resp_or_error do
      {:ok, %Req.Response{} = r} ->
        r

      %Req.Response{} = r ->
        r

      {:error, error} ->
        raise """
        ReqCassette: Network request failed

        Error: #{inspect(error)}

        This error occurred while trying to record a cassette. Make sure the server is running
        or use mode: :replay to use existing cassettes without hitting the network.
        """

      other ->
        raise "unexpected response format: #{inspect(other)}"
    end
  end

  defp forward_and_capture(conn, body, _opts) do
    # Convert Plug.Conn to a Req request and run it
    method = conn.method |> String.downcase() |> String.to_atom()
    headers = conn.req_headers

    # Build a full URL from conn
    # Use conn.scheme if available, otherwise infer from port
    scheme = to_string(conn.scheme || if(conn.port == 443, do: "https", else: "http"))
    host = conn.host || "localhost"
    port = conn.port || 80

    full =
      URI.to_string(%URI{
        scheme: scheme,
        host: host,
        port: port,
        path: conn.request_path,
        query: conn.query_string
      })

    # Create request options
    req_opts = [method: method, url: full, headers: headers]

    # Add body if present
    req_opts =
      if body != "" do
        req_opts ++ [body: body]
      else
        req_opts
      end

    # Create a new Req without the plug option to avoid infinite recursion
    req = Req.new(adapter: &Steps.run_finch/1)

    resp = Req.request(req, req_opts)
    {conn, resp}
  end

  defp resp_to_conn(conn, %{status: status, headers: headers, body: body}) do
    conn
    |> put_resp_headers(headers)
    |> send_resp(status, serialize_body(body))
    |> Conn.halt()
  end

  defp serialize_body(body) when is_binary(body), do: body

  defp serialize_body(body) do
    # for map/struct/list — convert to JSON
    Jason.encode!(body)
  end

  defp put_resp_headers(conn, headers) do
    Enum.reduce(headers, conn, fn {k, v_list}, acc ->
      # ensure header name and value are binaries
      value =
        case v_list do
          [v] when is_binary(v) ->
            v

          vs when is_list(vs) ->
            vs
            |> Enum.filter(&is_binary/1)
            |> Enum.join(", ")

          v when is_binary(v) ->
            v

          other ->
            # fallback: convert to string
            to_string(other)
        end

      Conn.put_resp_header(acc, k, value)
    end)
  end
end

1	defmodule ReqCassette.Filter do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Filters sensitive data from cassette interactions before saving.
4	
5	  This module provides comprehensive filtering capabilities to remove or redact sensitive
6	  information (API keys, tokens, passwords, etc.) from cassette files before they're saved.
7	  This ensures that cassettes can be safely committed to version control without exposing secrets.
8	
9	  ## Why Filter Cassettes?
10	
11	  Cassettes record real HTTP interactions, which often contain sensitive data:
12	
13	  - API keys in query strings or headers
14	  - Authentication tokens in request/response bodies
15	  - Session cookies in response headers
16	  - Personal information (emails, names, addresses)
17	  - Internal URLs or infrastructure details
18	
19	  Filtering prevents these secrets from being committed to your repository.
20	
21	  ## Filtering Types
22	
23	  ReqCassette supports four complementary filtering approaches:
24	
25	  ### 1. Regex-Based Replacement ✅ Recommended for patterns
26	
27	  Replace patterns in URIs, query strings, and request/response bodies using regular expressions:
28	
29	      filters = [
30	        filter_sensitive_data: [
31	          {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"},
32	          {~r/"token":"[^"]+"/, ~s("token":"<REDACTED>")},
33	          {~r/Bearer [\\w.-]+/, "Bearer <REDACTED>"}
34	        ]
35	      ]
36	
37	  **Features:**
38	  - Applied to URIs, query strings, and all body types
39	  - Works with both string and JSON bodies
40	  - For JSON bodies, tries pattern matching on serialized form first, then recursive matching
41	  - Multiple patterns processed in order
42	
43	  **Common patterns:**
44	  ```elixir
45	  # API keys
46	  {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"}
47	  {~r/"apiKey":"[^"]+"/, ~s("apiKey":"<REDACTED>")}
48	
49	  # Tokens
50	  {~r/Bearer [\\w.-]+/, "Bearer <REDACTED>"}
51	  {~r/"token":"[^"]+"/, ~s("token":"<REDACTED>")}
52	
53	  # Email addresses
54	  {~r/[\\w.+-]+@[\\w.-]+\\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}/, "user@example.com"}
55	
56	  # Credit cards
57	  {~r/\\d{4}[- ]?\\d{4}[- ]?\\d{4}[- ]?\\d{4}/, "XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX"}
58	
59	  # UUIDs (for consistent cassettes)
60	  {~r/[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}/, "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"}
61	  ```
62	
63	  ### 2. Header Removal ✅ Recommended for auth headers
64	
65	  Remove sensitive headers from requests and responses:
66	
67	      filters = [
68	        filter_request_headers: ["authorization", "x-api-key", "cookie"],
69	        filter_response_headers: ["set-cookie", "x-secret-token"]
70	      ]
71	
72	  **Features:**
73	  - Case-insensitive matching (`Authorization` matches `authorization`)
74	  - Completely removes headers from cassette
75	  - Separate lists for request and response headers
76	
77	  ### 3. Request Callback Filtering ✅ Safe for complex request filtering
78	
79	  Target request-only filtering with custom logic:
80	
81	      filters = [
82	        filter_request: fn request ->
83	          request
84	          |> update_in(["body_json", "email"], fn _ -> "redacted@example.com" end)
85	          |> update_in(["body_json", "timestamp"], fn _ -> "<NORMALIZED>" end)
86	        end
87	      ]
88	
89	  **Features:**
90	  - Applied during BOTH recording and matching (like regex/header filters)
91	  - Only receives request portion of interaction
92	  - Safe for complex request transformations
93	
94	  **⚠️ Important:** If `filter_request` modifies fields used for matching
95	  (method, uri, query, headers, body), consider adjusting `match_requests_on`
96	  to exclude those fields, or ensure transformations are idempotent.
97	
98	  **When to use:**
99	  - Complex request body transformations
100	  - Conditional filtering based on request fields
101	  - Normalization that can't be expressed as regex
102	
103	  **Request structure:**
104	  ```elixir
105	  %{
106	    "method" => "POST",
107	    "uri" => "https://...",
108	    "query_string" => "...",
109	    "headers" => %{},
110	    "body_type" => "json",
111	    "body_json" => %{}  # or "body" for text, "body_blob" for binary
112	  }
113	  ```
114	
115	  ### 4. Response Callback Filtering ✅ Always safe
116	
117	  Target response-only filtering:
118	
119	      filters = [
120	        filter_response: fn response ->
121	          response
122	          |> update_in(["body_json", "secret"], fn _ -> "<REDACTED>" end)
123	          |> update_in(["headers", "set-cookie"], fn _ -> ["<REDACTED>"] end)
124	        end
125	      ]
126	
127	  **Features:**
128	  - Applied ONLY during recording
129	  - Only receives response portion of interaction
130	  - Always safe - responses don't affect matching
131	  - Simplest callback type
132	
133	  **When to use:**
134	  - Response-only filtering
135	  - Complex response transformations
136	  - Conditional filtering based on response data
137	
138	  **Response structure:**
139	  ```elixir
140	  %{
141	    "status" => 200,
142	    "headers" => %{},
143	    "body_type" => "json",
144	    "body_json" => %{}  # or "body" for text, "body_blob" for binary
145	  }
146	  ```
147	
148	  ## Filter Application Order
149	
150	  Filters are applied in this specific order during recording:
151	
152	  1. **Regex filters** (`filter_sensitive_data`) - Applied to:
153	     - Request URI
154	     - Request query_string
155	     - Request body (all types: json, text, blob)
156	     - Response body (all types: json, text, blob)
157	
158	  2. **Header filters** - Applied to:
159	     - Request headers (`filter_request_headers`)
160	     - Response headers (`filter_response_headers`)
161	
162	  3. **Request callback** (`filter_request`) - Applied to:
163	     - Request only (entire request object)
164	
165	  4. **Response callback** (`filter_response`) - Applied to:
166	     - Response only (entire response object)
167	
168	  5. **Full interaction callback** (`before_record`) - Applied to:
169	     - Entire interaction (both request AND response)
170	     - See main module docs for warnings about this advanced option
171	
172	  This ordering ensures coarse-grained filters (regex, headers) run first, then
173	  specific callbacks (request/response), and finally the advanced `before_record`
174	  can access the complete filtered result.
175	
176	  ## Choosing the Right Filter Type
177	
178	  | Need                               | Recommended Approach            |
179	  |------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
180	  | Remove auth headers                | ✅ `filter_request_headers`     |
181	  | Redact API keys in URLs            | ✅ `filter_sensitive_data`      |
182	  | Redact tokens in JSON              | ✅ `filter_sensitive_data`      |
183	  | Complex request normalization      | ✅ `filter_request`             |
184	  | Complex response filtering         | ✅ `filter_response`            |
185	
186	  ## Usage
187	
188	      # Typically used via with_cassette/3
189	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
190	        "api_call",
191	        [
192	          # Regex patterns (fastest)
193	          filter_sensitive_data: [
194	            {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"}
195	          ],
196	
197	          # Header removal
198	          filter_request_headers: ["authorization"],
199	          filter_response_headers: ["set-cookie"],
200	
201	          # Request filtering (custom logic)
202	          filter_request: fn request ->
203	            update_in(request, ["body_json", "timestamp"], fn _ -> "<NORMALIZED>" end)
204	          end,
205	
206	          # Response filtering (always safe!)
207	          filter_response: fn response ->
208	            update_in(response, ["body_json", "secret"], fn _ -> "<REDACTED>" end)
209	          end
210	        ],
211	        fn plug ->
212	          Req.get!("https://api.example.com/data?api_key=secret123", plug: plug)
213	        end
214	      )
215	
216	      # Can also be used directly (internal API)
217	      filtered_interaction = ReqCassette.Filter.apply_filters(interaction, opts)
218	
219	  ## Examples
220	
221	      # Filter API keys from query strings
222	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
223	        "github_api",
224	        [
225	          filter_sensitive_data: [
226	            {~r/access_token=[\\w-]+/, "access_token=<REDACTED>"}
227	          ]
228	        ],
229	        fn plug ->
230	          Req.get!("https://api.github.com/user?access_token=gho_abc123", plug: plug)
231	        end
232	      )
233	      # Cassette will contain: ?access_token=<REDACTED>
234	
235	      # Remove authorization headers
236	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
237	        "authenticated_api",
238	        [filter_request_headers: ["authorization"]],
239	        fn plug ->
240	          Req.get!(
241	            "https://api.example.com/data",
242	            headers: [{"authorization", "Bearer secret"}],
243	            plug: plug
244	          )
245	        end
246	      )
247	      # Cassette won't contain the authorization header
248	
249	      # Filter tokens from JSON responses
250	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
251	        "login",
252	        [
253	          filter_sensitive_data: [
254	            {~r/"access_token":"[^"]+"/, ~s("access_token":"<REDACTED>")},
255	            {~r/"refresh_token":"[^"]+"/, ~s("refresh_token":"<REDACTED>")}
256	          ]
257	        ],
258	        fn plug ->
259	          Req.post!("https://auth.example.com/login", json: %{...}, plug: plug)
260	        end
261	      )
262	      # Tokens in response JSON are redacted
263	
264	      # Filter request with custom callback
265	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
266	        "normalized_request",
267	        [
268	          filter_request: fn request ->
269	            request
270	            # Normalize timestamp for consistent matching
271	            |> update_in(["body_json", "timestamp"], fn _ -> "<NORMALIZED>" end)
272	            # Redact email in request
273	            |> update_in(["body_json", "email"], fn _ -> "user@example.com" end)
274	          end
275	        ],
276	        fn plug ->
277	          Req.post!(
278	            "https://api.example.com/events",
279	            json: %{event: "login", timestamp: DateTime.utc_now(), email: "alice@example.com"},
280	            plug: plug
281	          )
282	        end
283	      )
284	
285	      # Filter response with custom callback
286	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
287	        "user_profile",
288	        [
289	          filter_response: fn response ->
290	            response
291	            # Redact email
292	            |> update_in(["body_json", "email"], fn _ -> "user@example.com" end)
293	            # Redact phone
294	            |> update_in(["body_json", "phone"], fn _ -> "555-0000" end)
295	            # Remove credit card completely
296	            |> update_in(["body_json"], &Map.delete(&1, "credit_card"))
297	          end
298	        ],
299	        fn plug ->
300	          Req.get!("https://api.example.com/profile", plug: plug)
301	        end
302	      )
303	
304	      # Combine all filter types
305	      ReqCassette.with_cassette(
306	        "complete_example",
307	        [
308	          # Regex filters for patterns
309	          filter_sensitive_data: [
310	            {~r/api_key=[\\w-]+/, "api_key=<REDACTED>"},
311	            {~r/"token":"[^"]+"/, ~s("token":"<REDACTED>")}
312	          ],
313	          # Header filters
314	          filter_request_headers: ["authorization", "cookie"],
315	          filter_response_headers: ["set-cookie", "x-api-key"],
316	          # Request callback for normalization
317	          filter_request: fn request ->
318	            update_in(request, ["body_json", "timestamp"], fn _ -> "<NORMALIZED>" end)
319	          end,
320	          # Response callback for redaction
321	          filter_response: fn response ->
322	            update_in(response, ["body_json", "user", "email"], fn _ ->
323	              "redacted@example.com"
324	            end)
325	          end
326	        ],
327	        fn plug ->
328	          Req.post!("https://api.example.com/data", json: %{...}, plug: plug)
329	        end
330	      )
331	
332	  ## JSON Body Handling
333	
334	  For JSON bodies, regex filters are applied intelligently:
335	
336	  1. First, try matching the pattern on the serialized JSON string
337	  2. If it matches, replace and attempt to parse back
338	  3. If parsing fails or pattern doesn't match, apply recursively to values
339	
340	  This allows patterns like `~r/"token":"[^"]+"` to match the JSON structure directly,
341	  while also supporting value-level patterns like `~r/secret_value/`.
342	
343	  ## Best Practices
344	
345	  - **Commit filtered cassettes** - Always filter before committing to version control
346	  - **Use regex for patterns** - API keys, tokens, and structured secrets
347	  - **Use headers for credentials** - Remove Authorization, Cookie headers
348	  - **Use filter_request for request normalization** - Timestamps, IDs, request-specific data
349	  - **Use filter_response for response redaction** - Safe and simple for all response filtering
350	  - **Test your filters** - Manually inspect cassettes after filtering
351	  - **Document patterns** - Comment your regex patterns for maintainability
352	  - **Be cautious with filter_request** - Ensure transformations are idempotent or adjust match_requests_on
353	
354	  ## See Also
355	
356	  - `ReqCassette` - Main module with examples
357	  - `ReqCassette.Cassette` - Cassette format and interaction structure
358	  """
359	
360	  @doc """
361	  Applies all configured filters to an interaction before saving.
362	
363	  ## Parameters
364	
365	  - `interaction` - The cassette interaction map
366	  - `opts` - Filter options from cassette configuration
367	    - `:filter_sensitive_data` - List of `{regex, replacement}` tuples
368	    - `:filter_request_headers` - List of header names to remove from requests
369	    - `:filter_response_headers` - List of header names to remove from responses
370	    - `:filter_request` - Callback function `(request -> request)` for request-only filtering
371	    - `:filter_response` - Callback function `(response -> response)` for response-only filtering
372	
373	  ## Filter Application Order
374	
375	  1. **Regex filters** - Applied to URI, query string, request body, response body
376	  2. **Header filters** - Remove specified request/response headers
377	  3. **Request callback** (filter_request) - Transform request
378	  4. **Response callback** (filter_response) - Transform response
379	
380	  ## Returns
381	
382	  Filtered interaction map
383	
384	  ## Note
385	
386	  This function also supports the advanced `:before_record` option for backward compatibility
387	  and special use cases. See `ReqCassette` module documentation for details on when to use it.
388	  """
389	  @spec apply_filters(map(), map()) :: map()
390	  def apply_filters(interaction, opts) do
391	    interaction
392	    |> apply_regex_filters(opts[:filter_sensitive_data] || [])
393	    |> apply_header_filters(
394	      opts[:filter_request_headers] || [],
395	      opts[:filter_response_headers] || []
396	    )
397	    |> apply_request_callback(opts[:filter_request])
398	    |> apply_response_callback(opts[:filter_response])
399	    |> apply_callback(opts[:before_record])
400	  end
401	
402	  @doc """
403	  Applies only response-related filters to an interaction.
404	
405	  Use this when the request has already been filtered at an earlier stage
406	  (e.g., in the plug before matching). This prevents non-idempotent filters
407	  from being applied twice to requests.
408	
409	  ## Filters Applied
410	
411	  - Regex filters (`filter_sensitive_data`) - response body only
412	  - Header filters (`filter_response_headers`) - response headers only
413	  - Response callback (`filter_response`)
414	  - Before record callback (`before_record`)
415	
416	  ## Filters NOT Applied
417	
418	  - Regex filters on request (already done)
419	  - Header filters on request headers (already done)
420	  - Request callback (`filter_request`) (already done)
421	  """
422	  @spec apply_response_only_filters(map(), map()) :: map()
423	  def apply_response_only_filters(interaction, opts) do
424	    interaction
425	    |> apply_regex_filters_response_only(opts[:filter_sensitive_data] || [])
426	    |> apply_response_header_filters(opts[:filter_response_headers] || [])
427	    |> apply_response_callback(opts[:filter_response])
428	    |> apply_callback(opts[:before_record])
429	  end
430	
431	  # Regex filters applied to response only (request already filtered)
432	  defp apply_regex_filters_response_only(interaction, patterns) do
433	    Enum.reduce(patterns, interaction, fn {pattern, replacement}, acc ->
434	      # Only apply to response body (request already filtered at entry point)
435	      update_body_in(acc, ["response"], fn body ->
436	        apply_regex_to_body(body, pattern, replacement)
437	      end)
438	    end)
439	  end
440	
441	  # Header filters applied to response only
442	  defp apply_response_header_filters(interaction, response_headers) do
443	    update_in(interaction, ["response", "headers"], fn headers ->
444	      remove_headers(headers, response_headers)
445	    end)
446	  end
447	
448	  # Regex-based pattern replacement
449	  defp apply_regex_filters(interaction, patterns) do
450	    Enum.reduce(patterns, interaction, fn {pattern, replacement}, acc ->
451	      acc
452	      # Apply to request body
453	      |> update_body_in(["request"], fn body ->
454	        apply_regex_to_body(body, pattern, replacement)
455	      end)
456	      # Apply to response body
457	      |> update_body_in(["response"], fn body ->
458	        apply_regex_to_body(body, pattern, replacement)
459	      end)
460	      # Also apply to URI and query_string
461	      |> update_in(["request", "uri"], fn uri ->
462	        if uri, do: Regex.replace(pattern, uri, replacement), else: uri
463	      end)
464	      |> update_in(["request", "query_string"], fn qs ->
465	        if qs, do: Regex.replace(pattern, qs, replacement), else: qs
466	      end)
467	    end)
468	  end
469	
470	  defp apply_regex_to_body(body, pattern, replacement) do
471	    cond do
472	      is_binary(body) ->
473	        Regex.replace(pattern, body, replacement)
474	
475	      is_map(body) or is_list(body) ->
476	        # For JSON bodies, try two approaches:
477	        # 1. Apply directly to values (for patterns like /value/)
478	        # 2. Apply to serialized JSON (for patterns like /"key":"value"/)
479	
480	        # First, try serializing to JSON and applying the pattern
481	        json = Jason.encode!(body)
482	
483	        if Regex.match?(pattern, json) do
484	          # Pattern matches the JSON format, so replace in serialized form
485	          replaced = Regex.replace(pattern, json, replacement)
486	
487	          # Try to parse back
488	          case Jason.decode(replaced) do
489	            {:ok, decoded} -> decoded
490	            {:error, _} -> body
491	          end
492	        else
493	          # Pattern doesn't match JSON format, apply recursively to values
494	          apply_regex_recursively(body, pattern, replacement)
495	        end
496	
497	      true ->
498	        body
499	    end
500	  end
501	
502	  defp apply_regex_recursively(body, pattern, replacement) when is_map(body) do
503	    Map.new(body, fn {key, value} ->
504	      new_value =
505	        cond do
506	          is_binary(value) -> Regex.replace(pattern, value, replacement)
507	          is_map(value) -> apply_regex_recursively(value, pattern, replacement)
508	          is_list(value) -> Enum.map(value, &apply_regex_recursively(&1, pattern, replacement))
509	          true -> value
510	        end
511	
512	      {key, new_value}
513	    end)
514	  end
515	
516	  defp apply_regex_recursively(body, pattern, replacement) when is_list(body) do
517	    Enum.map(body, &apply_regex_recursively(&1, pattern, replacement))
518	  end
519	
520	  defp apply_regex_recursively(body, pattern, replacement) when is_binary(body) do
521	    Regex.replace(pattern, body, replacement)
522	  end
523	
524	  defp apply_regex_recursively(body, _pattern, _replacement), do: body
525	
526	  # Header removal/redaction
527	  defp apply_header_filters(interaction, request_headers, response_headers) do
528	    interaction
529	    |> update_in(["request", "headers"], fn headers ->
530	      remove_headers(headers, request_headers)
531	    end)
532	    |> update_in(["response", "headers"], fn headers ->
533	      remove_headers(headers, response_headers)
534	    end)
535	  end
536	
537	  defp remove_headers(headers, headers_to_remove) do
538	    lowercase_remove = Enum.map(headers_to_remove, &String.downcase/1)
539	
540	    Enum.reject(headers, fn {key, _value} ->
541	      String.downcase(key) in lowercase_remove
542	    end)
543	    |> Enum.into(%{})
544	  end
545	
546	  # Request-only callback filtering
547	  defp apply_request_callback(interaction, nil), do: interaction
548	
549	  defp apply_request_callback(interaction, callback) when is_function(callback, 1) do
550	    update_in(interaction, ["request"], callback)
551	  end
552	
553	  defp apply_request_callback(interaction, _), do: interaction
554	
555	  # Response-only callback filtering
556	  defp apply_response_callback(interaction, nil), do: interaction
557	
558	  defp apply_response_callback(interaction, callback) when is_function(callback, 1) do
559	    update_in(interaction, ["response"], callback)
560	  end
561	
562	  defp apply_response_callback(interaction, _), do: interaction
563	
564	  # Full interaction callback filtering
565	  defp apply_callback(interaction, nil), do: interaction
566	
567	  defp apply_callback(interaction, callback) when is_function(callback, 1) do
568	    callback.(interaction)
569	  end
570	
571	  defp apply_callback(interaction, _), do: interaction
572	
573	  # Helper to update body fields regardless of body type
574	  defp update_body_in(interaction, path, fun) do
575	    # Body could be in "body", "body_json", or "body_blob"
576	    cond do
577	      get_in(interaction, path ++ ["body"]) ->
578	        update_in(interaction, path ++ ["body"], fun)
579	
580	      get_in(interaction, path ++ ["body_json"]) ->
581	        update_in(interaction, path ++ ["body_json"], fun)
582	
583	      get_in(interaction, path ++ ["body_blob"]) ->
584	        # For blob, decode, apply filter, re-encode
585	        update_in(interaction, path ++ ["body_blob"], fn blob ->
586	          decoded = Base.decode64!(blob)
587	          filtered = fun.(decoded)
588	          Base.encode64(filtered)
589	        end)
590	
591	      true ->
592	        interaction
593	    end
594	  end
595	end
